ai.title: Fix edit tool diff rendering
ai.summary: Added `shouldShowEditDiff` helper to gate diff preview rendering in `str-replace.tsx`. Prevents create operations from flashing input-derived full-file diffs by waiting for tool result output. Scope limited to CLI components and implementor helpers.

eli5.text: When you create or edit a file, the screen no longer briefly shows a confusing before-and-after diff before the change finishes. The diff preview now waits to appear until the edit actually completes, so you will not see a misleading full-file flash during create operations. This affects anyone watching the edit process in the command-line interface.

ai.title: Clarify string tool input errors
ai.summary: Tool executor error messages updated in `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/tool-executor.ts`. Logic distinguishes between JSON parsing failure and successful parsing yielding a string. Scope limited to Agent Runtime tool execution surface.

eli5.text: When the assistant asks a tool to do something, you send instructions as a list of settings. If you accidentally send that list as one long piece of text instead of structured data, the assistant has started giving you a clearer message about what went wrong. It now tells you plainly whether your instructions couldn't be read as structured data or were just plain text, and reminds you to send the full set of settings in the right format. This applies to anyone interacting with the assistant's tool use, and is live today.

ai.title: Fix duplicate reviewer agent card
ai.summary: Fix duplicate reviewer agent cards by propagating `realAgentType` through `resolveSpawnAgentToReal` and `moveSpawnAgentBlock` in the CLI, and normalizing agent IDs via `normalizeAgentIdForLookup` in the Agent Runtime `tool-executor.ts`. This ensures spawned agents correctly map to their real types and IDs during event handling and execution, preventing UI duplication. Scope includes `cli/src/utils/message-block-helpers.ts`, `sdk-event-handlers.ts`, `spawn-agent-matcher.ts`, and `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/tool-executor.ts`. `getAgentBaseName` now replaces underscores with hyphens to match normalized IDs.

eli5.text: When the CLI runs a sub-agent (like the reviewer agent in a multi-step coding plan), it sometimes rendered two identical agent cards in the conversation panel. The CLI now carries the spawned agent's real type and ID all the way through the event-handling path, and normalizes identifiers (treating underscores and hyphens as the same) so each sub-agent matches only one UI block instead of duplicating. This fix is live today for CLI users running plans that spawn reviewer or other named sub-agents.

ai.title: Freebuff 1.0.669 release bump
ai.summary: This release bundles a day of user-visible work landed since 1.0.668 under a single version tag. Among the most significant additions, `str_replace` and `propose_str_replace` tool parameters were renamed from `old`/`new` to `oldString`/`newString` to match Cursor-style schemas and avoid keyword collisions, and Agent Runtime tool call ids are now deterministic (`functions.<toolName>:<index>`) instead of random UUIDs, stabilizing retries and re-parses. Other notable ships include a shared premium session quota (5 sessions, Pacific-midnight reset) surfaced in the CLI model selector, status bar, and waiting room; a free-tier `browser-use` agent mapped to `google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview`; DeepSeek image attachment handling that strips unsupported `image_url`/`file` parts; CLI takeover prompts for concurrent instances; keyboard navigation in the waiting room; grouped code search output with a global match count; and a fix ensuring thinker-style final output via `lastMessage` renders when no text blocks were streamed. The change here is purely the manifest bump, `cli/release/package.json` version field.
ai.evidence: Commit e55b1d5c modifies only `cli/release/package.json`, bumping `codebuff.version` from 1.0.668 to 1.0.669 with no code changes (diff is +1/-1 in the version field only).

eli5.text: This release adds a lot of helpful polish to how you use Freebuff every day. First, your premium AI quota (DeepSeek, Kimi, and GLM) now resets each night at midnight Pacific time, so you no longer have to remember a rolling 20-hour window, and the CLI shows your shared session count instead of confusing per-model limits. Second, the waiting room and model picker now react properly to your keyboard (arrows, Tab, Enter) so you can take over or exit cleanly when another session is running. Third, thinker-style agents now display their final answer in the CLI instead of hiding it when tools are used. Fourth, browser automation (the browser-use agent) is now available even in free mode, so free users can run web tasks. Fifth, image/file attachments you send to DeepSeek are now safely converted to a text notice instead of breaking the request. On top of that, code search results now group matches by file with line numbers and a total count, duplicate reviewer agent cards are fixed, and error messages for string inputs are clearer. Altogether, upgrading means less guessing about quotas, smoother keyboard-driven flow, correct display of agent outputs, and fewer annoying glitches across free and premium tiers.

ai.title: Freebuff 0.0.78 bundles DeepSeek image handling, deterministic tool
ai.summary: Version 0.0.78 rolls up a day of user-visible work landed since 0.0.77 into a single release tag. Among the most significant additions, str_replace and propose_str_replace tool parameters were renamed from old/new to oldString/newString to match Cursor-style schemas and avoid keyword collisions, and Agent Runtime tool call ids are now deterministic (functions.<toolName>:<index>) instead of random UUIDs, stabilizing retries and re-parses. Other notable ships include DeepSeek image attachment handling that strips unsupported image_url/file parts via a new deepseek-request-body.ts normalizer, a free-tier browser-use agent mapped to google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview, CLI takeover prompts for concurrent instances, keyboard navigation in the waiting room, grouped code search output with a global match count, and a fix ensuring thinker-style final output via lastMessage renders when no text blocks were streamed. The change here is purely the manifest bump in freebuff/cli/release/package.json.
ai.evidence: Diff hunk in freebuff/cli/release/package.json changes the version field from 0.0.77 to 0.0.78, matching the release-bump commit nature and the earlier same-day commit e55b1d5c Freebuff 1.0.669 release bump pattern. Analysis notes confirm this is a version bump to 0.0.78 bundling a day of user-visible work since 0.0.77.

eli5.text: This release adds support for attaching images to your conversations with DeepSeek, enables browser automation tools for free users, and makes the command-line experience smoother and more reliable. Free users can now use browser automation capabilities powered by Google's Gemini model, premium sessions reset daily at Pacific midnight instead of every 20 hours, and starting a second instance prompts you to take over or exit rather than silently conflicting. Tool calls use stable, predictable identifiers instead of random ones for more consistent behavior, and search results are grouped by file with clearer formatting. Upgrading means smoother multi-window usage, clearer error messages, better keyboard navigation in menus, and more reliable agent behavior when things need to be retried.

ai.title: Fix Freebuff CLI auth code handling
ai.summary: Auth code parsing switched from naive split to lastIndexOf extraction to handle identifiers containing dots. Login URL generation now derives origin from request URL instead of env var, preventing apex/www host bouncing. Changes applied to both freebuff/web and web packages. Added warning logs for invalid auth code attempts.

eli5.text: When you type a code from the Freebuff command-line tool into your browser to log in, the system now reads that code correctly even if parts of it contain dots, which previously could get it split in the wrong places. The link your browser opens is now built from the exact address the code came from, instead of a default address that sometimes sent you to the wrong version of the site (apex vs. www) during sign-in. If your code still doesn't match, the system now records a warning with details about the parts it expected versus what you entered, helping spot typos or copy mistakes. It's live today for anyone using the Freebuff CLI sign-in flow.

ai.title: CLI auto-takeover for dead Freebuff sessions
ai.summary: CLI now auto-takeover stale Freebuff sessions if the previous owner process is dead. New `freebuff-instance-owner.ts` tracks local PID in config dir to detect zombie seats. `use-freebuff-session.ts` checks this state before prompting, switching to silent POST if stale. Exit handler updated to call `exitFreebuffCleanly` for Freebuff instances.

eli5.text: When you use Freebuff and start a new session, the CLI will now automatically take over a previous session if it belonged to your own process that has since died, instead of asking you to confirm. It does this by leaving a small record on disk with the process ID of the current session owner; before you're asked to take over, it checks whether that process is still alive, and if it's a zombie (dead), it silently completes the takeover itself. This only applies to your local Freebuff sessions; if the stale session belonged to another running process or another account, it still asks you first. Live today for Freebuff users.

ai.title: Add Freebuff session restart option
ai.summary: Added a session restart option to the CLI session-ended banner, allowing users to start a new same-chat session or pick a new model. The `use-freebuff-session` hook was updated to re-POST with the fallback model on unavailability to prevent stuck pending states. Changes are scoped to the CLI components and hooks, specifically `session-ended-banner.tsx`, `use-freebuff-session.ts`, and `use-send-message.ts`.

eli5.text: When your freechat session ends, a banner now appears offering you a way to start fresh. Pressing Enter begins a new same-chat session, while Esc takes you back to pick a different model. Behind the scenes, the system re-sends your request with a fallback model instead of redisplaying the old ended row, which prevents the banner from getting stuck if the original model was unavailable. This keeps the conversation flowing without leaving you waiting on a dead session.

ai.title: Signup credit grant added, 500 one-time, replacing monthly default
ai.summary: New accounts now receive a one-time 500-credit signup grant via `grantSignupCredits`, driven by the new `SIGNUP_FREE_CREDITS_GRANT` constant, while the recurring monthly default `DEFAULT_FREE_CREDITS_GRANT` drops to 0. The monthly reset path in `packages/billing/src/grant-credits.ts` now issues grandfathered credits only to users with a prior expired free grant, replacing `getPreviousFreeGrantAmount` with `getGrandfatheredFreeGrantAmount` which returns 0 when none exist. This shifts the free-credit model from a per-cycle default to a one-time signup bonus plus grandfathered monthly resets. A `signup-free-${userId}` deterministic operation id is used for idempotent granting.
ai.evidence: In `common/src/constants/limits.ts`, `DEFAULT_FREE_CREDITS_GRANT` changed from 500 to 0 and a new `SIGNUP_FREE_CREDITS_GRANT = 500` was added; in `packages/billing/src/grant-credits.ts`, `getPreviousFreeGrantAmount` was replaced by `getGrandfatheredFreeGrantAmount` (returning 0 when no prior expired free grant exists) and `grantSignupCredits` was added, which is invoked from the `createUser` event in `web/src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/auth-options.ts`; `common/src/constants/limits.ts`, `packages/billing/src/grant-credits.ts`, `packages/billing/src/billing.knowledge.md`, `packages/billing/src/grant-credits.knowledge.md`.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show whether the `signup-free-${userId}` operation id is consumed by any downstream reporting or whether the pricing page and usage display reflect the new grant grouping at runtime. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

changes.what: Added `grantSignupCredits` function using `signup-free-${userId}` operation id and replaced `getPreviousFreeGrantAmount` with `getGrandfatheredFreeGrantAmount` returning 0 when no prior expired grant exists.
Calls `grantSignupCredits` in the `createUser` event after replacing the previous comment that new accounts receive no signup bonus.
Simplified the out-of-credits message by removing the reset countdown string.
Updated grant type documentation to describe free grants as both signup and grandfathered monthly credits.
Clarified that grandfathered monthly free grants and legacy referral grants use next reset date for operation ids.

ai.title: CLI model selector grouped by tier
ai.summary: Premium and Unlimited models now render in grouped sections within the CLI model selector, replacing per-row tier chips. The shared 0/5 quota counter moved to the PREMIUM section header. Layout adjustments include column-aligned names and explicit flexbox containers in the waiting room screen for landing and queued states. Empty sections are filtered out to prevent orphan headers.

eli5.text: When you open the model picker in the Freebuff CLI, paid-tier models now appear together under a single PREMIUM heading (showing one shared 0/5 quota counter) instead of each row carrying its own "Premium" or "Unlimited" label, and empty tiers are hidden so you never see an orphan header. The waiting-room screen also got layout tweaks so the landing and queued states line up neatly in their own flexible containers.

ai.title: Freebuff 0.0.79 ships auth, session, model picker, and signup credit
ai.summary: Version 0.0.79 rolls up the day's user-visible CLI and web improvements shipped since 0.0.78. Auth code parsing now uses lastIndexOf extraction in freebuff/web and web packages, fixing logins when identifiers contain dots, and login URL origin derives from the request URL instead of an env var. The CLI auto-takeovers stale sessions by tracking a local PID in freebuff-instance-owner.ts and re-POSTs with the fallback model to prevent stuck pending states, and adds a session restart option on the session-ended banner in session-ended-banner.tsx. New accounts receive a one-time 500-credit SIGNUP_FREE_CREDITS_GRANT replacing monthly grants, with grandfathered users still on monthly cycles via getGrandfatheredFreeGrantAmount in packages/billing/src/grant-credits.ts. The CLI model selector groups Premium and Unlimited models into tiered sections, moving the shared 0/5 premium session quota counter to the PREMIUM section header and filtering empty sections to avoid orphan headers.
ai.evidence: Diff hunk in freebuff/cli/release/package.json changes the "version" field from "0.0.78" to "0.0.79". Analysis notes list this commit as a release-bump tagged as Packaging, with release instructions directing summarizers to use the bundled user-visible updates since 0.0.78 rather than the version number change alone.

eli5.text: Freebuff 0.0.79 makes signing up and getting started easier, keeps your sessions running smoothly, and makes choosing AI models more intuitive. New users now get a one-time signup credit of 500 Freebuff credits instead of monthly grants, while existing users keep their current credits through grandfathered support. The login process is more reliable and secure, handling tricky login codes without breaking and preventing website redirect issues. If your session ever stalls or times out, the app can now automatically take over an abandoned session instead of leaving you stuck, and a new restart option lets you begin a fresh conversation or switch models from the ended-session screen. The model picker now groups premium and unlimited models into clear sections with a shared quota counter, so it's easier to see what's available at a glance. Upgrading gives you smoother logins, uninterrupted sessions, clearer model choices, and a simpler credit system that rewards new users upfront.

ai.title: Move premium session counter to waiting room title
ai.summary: Removed section header counter and related logic from `freebuff-model-selector.tsx`, moving the premium session quota display to the page title in `waiting-room-screen.tsx`. The selector now purely lists models grouped by tier, while the waiting room screen imports `FREEBUFF_PREMIUM_SESSION_LIMIT` and calculates remaining sessions to display in the header text. This consolidates quota visibility outside the interactive selection list.

eli5.text: When you're waiting in the Freebuff CLI queue and pick from the paid model list, the remaining paid-session count (for example 3/5) now appears in the waiting-room title line instead of inside the model-selector section header. Free-tiers still just list models without any quota display, and when your paid allowance hits zero the count turns amber so it reads as you've hit the limit rather than just another number. The selector itself is now purely a list of choices grouped by tier, while the waiting-room screen imports the shared session limit and calculates the remaining quota to show in its header text. Note: the analyzer tagged this as minor, and there are several sibling changes in this snapshot that are unrelated housekeeping like fixing diff rendering and version bumps.

ai.title: Freebuff 0.0.80 release bakes in waiting-room quota tally
ai.summary: Version 0.0.80 rolls up the preceding same-day stabilization work, most visibly the migration of the premium session quota counter from the model-list section header into the waiting-room page title, so `freebuff-model-selector.tsx` now pure-lists tier-grouped models while `waiting-room-screen.tsx` imports `FREEBUFF_PREMIUM_SESSION_LIMIT` and renders remaining sessions in the header text. The package manifest in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` is bumped from 0.0.79 to 0.0.80, matching the release-bump cadence that bundles CLI auth code parsing, stale-session auto-takeover, signup credit grant, and deterministic tool call id changes shipped earlier in the day.
ai.evidence: Commit [35fc6088] modifies `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` to bump the `version` field from `0.0.79` to `0.0.80` (+1/-1 lines), following the same-day release-bump pattern seen in commits [6a13c460] and [6ebbb915].

eli5.text: Freebuff 0.0.80 makes it clearer how many premium AI sessions you have left before you hit your limit. Instead of showing a quota counter inside the model selection screen, the app now displays your remaining premium sessions right in the waiting room title, so you always see your balance up front. This means the model picker stays focused on listing available models by tier without mixing in quota tracking. Upgrading gives you a simpler, at-a-glance view of your usage status while still keeping all the same models and features intact.
